messages:
Iris: hi all, day 2 at Redwood. trying to get my dev flow working across M1 Mac + Windows laptop. main pain: dotfiles sync + asdf versions + signing commits. TL;DR: what's the minimal setup that doesn't blow up switching machines?

Kai: congrats! short answer: pick a canonical place for your shell runtime and keep tooling there. if you plan to edit in VSCode on both, Remote-WSL (windows) and native (mac) are the usual combo. what are you using for dotfiles?

Iris: bare repo + a few stow symlinks. asdf for node/python. using fish on mac, bash in WSL. i tried to keep the same $HOME layout but symlinks behave differently on NTFS.

Jordan: yeah NTFS + symlinks = headache. two patterns that work: 1) make WSL your authoritative home (clone dotfiles in WSL), use stow from WSL, and have VSCode connect Remote-WSL; 2) use chezmoi with templates to generate OS-specific files. both keep things simple across platforms.

Maya: if you prefer fish, ensure you have a platform check in dotfiles. e.g. in your install script: `if uname | grep -iq darwin; then install fish for mac; elif grep -iq microsoft /proc/version; then install fish in WSL; fi` . also add `core.autocrlf = input` to avoid CRLF surprises.

Iris: i have trouble with commit signing. i sign commits with GPG on mac; on windows commits from the GUI fail to sign with `gpg: signing failed: No pinentry`. any tips?

Kai: common cause is the GUI using Windows git while your gpg lives in WSL. options: run git from same environment as gpg (use Remote-WSL), or set up Gpg4win and import the key there, or use SSH-based signatures if org allows. also ensure `git config gpg.program` points to the proper gpg binary and `export GPG_TTY=$(tty)` in shell.

Jordan: another neat trick: if you use 1Password for keys, run the op CLI inside the environment used by git. on mac `eval $(op agent --enable)`. in WSL install the linux `op` and `op signin`. that makes the agent socket available to the runtime.

Maya: direnv gotchas: files created/edited in Windows sometimes have CRLF so direnv invalidates the signature and keeps asking for `direnv allow`. run `git config core.autocrlf input` and `dos2unix .envrc` if needed. also check your shell hook is installed: `eval "$(direnv hook fish)"` or bash/zsh hook in the right dotfile.

Iris: ok. i also see weird PATH differences — brew on M1 is /opt/homebrew. sometimes node installed by asdf isn't first. any ordering advice?

Kai: on mac put `/opt/homebrew/bin` earlier in PATH in .profile/.zprofile. ensure `source ~/.asdf/asdf.sh` and `source ~/.asdf/completions/asdf.bash` in whichever shell you use. run `asdf reshim` after adding plugins. in WSL you might need `sudo apt install libssl-dev zlib1g-dev` before building certain versions.

Jordan: small practical checklist I give new hires: 1) choose authoritative runtime (WSL or native mac), 2) ensure editor uses that runtime (Remote-WSL or native VSCode), 3) put key agents (ssh/gpg/op) in same runtime, 4) set core.autocrlf properly, 5) add OS notes in dotfiles README, 6) run `asdf reshim` and check PATH order.

Iris: perfect. i'm going to: make WSL authoritative on my Windows laptop, move dotfiles install to WSL, install op in WSL, fix core.autocrlf, and use Remote-WSL for VSCode. i'll try that and report back.

Maya: also ping devex if you want pair debugging. we do weekly onboarding hours too.

Iris: thanks all, saved me multiple hours already :smile:
